newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Apple & Pear Board faces tough yr - EEC.
newsitem.headline: NZ Apple & Pear Board faces tough yr - EEC.

text.p: Eastern Equities Corp Ltd (EEC) on Wednesday warned that the New Zealand Apple and Pear Marketing Board faced a challenging task if it was to achieve increased returns this year over those for 1996.
EEC, which reported a NZ$42,000 loss for the six months to February 28, said opening prices for Southern Hemisphere fruit in 1997 had been mixed.
"New Zealand's early season fruit has generally been smaller than last year," EEC said.

"This, together with large carry-over stocks of Northern Hemisphere fruit, larger than anticipated South American production coming on stream, and the continuing strong Kiwi dollar will impact on the board's early sales receipts."
EEC Horticulture Ltd (EEH) incurred an operating loss of NZ$3.22 million in the half year.

EEC said Hawkes Bay had experienced one of its most difficult growing seasons ever, with higher than normal summer rainfall and a devastating series of hail strikes which had made orchard husbandry difficult and severely affected packout rates for the region.
"The hail effect in EEH's Hastings orchards has reduced the estimated export packout to 464,000 export TCEs (Tray Carton Equivalents) -- a 37 percent reduction from original forecasts," EEC said.
It said the New Zealand export apple crop was originally estimated to be 19.8 million TCEs for the 1996/97 season -- the current forecast was for an export crop of around 15.1 million TCEs.

"The New Zealand Apple and Pear Marketing Board has a challenging task to achieve increased returns over those for 1996 even though the crop is 16 percent lower, particularly as there is no apparent decrease in its cost structures in the key areas of cool storage, shipping and logistics management," EEC said.
